source: OECD (2025), Health at a Glance 2025: OECD Indicators, OECD Publishing, Paris
framing: Gap framing: every figure is what is NOT covered, NOT satisfied or unmet. Gap figures are 100 minus the published figure.
rule: HAL may phrase these facts freely but must not state any figure, ranking or claim that is not in this list. Verbatim report sentences may name other countries; only what they say about this country may be used.

facts.text: 38% of people in Spain were NOT satisfied with the availability of quality healthcare where they live in 2024, versus an OECD average of 36%; satisfaction has deteriorated over the past decade.
26.8% of health spending in Spain was NOT covered by government or compulsory insurance schemes in 2023, versus an OECD average of 24.9%.
1.8% of people in Spain reported unmet medical care needs due to cost, distance or waiting times in 2024 (average of 28 OECD countries: 3.4%).
4% of hospital care costs in Spain were NOT covered by public or compulsory schemes in 2023, versus 11% on average in the OECD.
16% of outpatient medical care costs in Spain were NOT covered by public or compulsory schemes in 2023, versus 22% on average in the OECD.
99% of dental care costs in Spain were NOT covered by public or compulsory schemes in 2023, versus 68% on average in the OECD.
33% of pharmaceutical costs in Spain were NOT covered by public or compulsory schemes in 2023, versus 42% on average in the OECD.
This is especially notable in Finland, Lithuania, Ireland, Greece, Spain and France, where unmet medical care needs due to waiting times increased by 1.4 percentage points or more since 2019.

In Spain, the National Health System established the Working Group on Waiting Lists (Grupo de Trabajo sobre Listas de Espera) to standardise management and reporting of waiting lists across the autonomous communities.

There are also some variations in the survey questions across countries: while most countries refer to both a medical examination and treatment, the question in some countries (Czechia and Spain) only refers to a medical examination or a doctor consultation, resulting in lower rates of unmet needs.
In terms of median number of days (Figure 5.11, right panel), this ranged from around 50 days or less in Spain, Poland, Hungary and Sweden, to 280 days in Slovenia.
In 2024, median waiting times ranged from 67 days in Sweden and Spain, to over half a year in Hungary (209 days), Chile (313 days), Poland (343 days), and almost two years in Slovenia (667 days).
Remote consultations cannot be distinguished and are included in a few countries (such as Austria from 2020, and Ireland, Japan, Latvia, the Netherlands, the Slovak Republic and Spain from 2019).
By contrast, countries including France, Slovenia and Spain have lower price levels, with the same healthcare basket costing roughly two-thirds of the OECD average.
